opportunities.title: Your Ledger Was Never the Backstop: Zilliqa App Bug Lets Attackers Pull Private Keys Straight Off the Device
opportunities.why_now: A hardware wallet vulnerability recovering signer keys is the nightmare scenario the 'just use cold storage' crowd insists can't happen — and it just did.
opportunities.angle: Security teardown: explain the exploit mechanics, then widen to 'hardware wallets are still software' thesis with a checklist of what self-custody actually requires post-Zilliqa.

opportunities.title: $31.6M, Two Bridges, Seven Hours: Bridges Are Still the Weakest Link and Nobody's Fixing It
opportunities.why_now: Two separate bridge exploits within hours of each other is a fresh, quotable data point for the 'bridges = free money for hackers' pattern that's been priced in since 2022.
opportunities.angle: Pattern-recognition post: timeline the two hacks side by side, tally cumulative bridge losses since 2021, and make the 'this was always going to happen again' case.

opportunities.title: Robinhood's CEO Got Rekt by a Memecoin Scam on His Own X Account — And That's the Best Case Scenario
opportunities.why_now: A high-profile exec account takeover pushing a scam token is a perfect vehicle to talk about account security failures at the exact companies selling you 'safe' crypto access.
opportunities.angle: Contrarian take: use the irony (Robinhood = 'safe' onramp, CEO hacked for a memecoin pump) to argue platform trust is theater; include a quick 2FA/account-hygiene checklist.

opportunities.title: SummerFi Just Died From an Exploit You Never Heard About — That's the Real Story
opportunities.why_now: A seven-year-old DeFi protocol shutting down 'citing exploit' with almost no coverage is exactly the quiet-death pattern this channel exists to flag before it becomes a headline elsewhere.
opportunities.angle: Investigative short: dig into what actually happened at SummerFi, why it didn't trend, and what that silence says about how many exploits get buried without disclosure.

opportunities.title: Arthur Hayes' 'Insider Trading Desk': BitMEX Winds Down the Same Way It Started — With Everyone Else's Money
opportunities.why_now: Fresh fraud claims against BitMEX co-founders as the exchange shuts down is a full-circle security/governance story with instant recognition and a built-in 'told you so.'
opportunities.angle: Explainer + retrospective: lay out the allegations, then trace BitMEX's history of regulatory run-ins to argue this ending was always the base rate for founder-controlled exchanges.
